name: navy-coder
description: AI coding assistant for VS Code — agentic tool-use, file edits with diff approval, multi-provider (Ollama, OpenAI, compatible APIs).

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In a workspace you have not trusted, Navy still opens and can read files and answer questions, but it will not run shell commands, start language toolchains, launch MCP servers, or send file contents to an embeddings provider.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Navy's file, search, and terminal tools need a real filesystem on disk.

navy.model.description: The model to use for chat. Leave empty to auto-select the first available model for the chosen provider (e.g. llama3, gpt-4o, claude-sonnet-4-6).

navy.host.description: Base URL of the inference server (Ollama, LM Studio, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint).

navy.systemPrompt.description: Optional custom instructions appended to every conversation (e.g. coding style preferences). Does not replace or override Navy's built-in tool-use rules.

navy.skills.description: Agent Skills: folders with a SKILL.md, read from .navy/skills/ and .claude/skills/ in the project and from Navy's global storage. "auto" offers every installed skill to the model; "off" loads none; an array of names offers only those. Every offered skill's name and description sits in EVERY request, so this is a real cost on a small local model — Navy caps the total against the model's own context window and says in the output channel which skills it left out. A skill never grants permission: its `allowed-tools` is shown but never honoured, and anything it runs or changes still goes through the approval gate.

navy.speechVoice.description: Exact name of the system voice used for Read Aloud. Empty picks the best voice installed for your language — on Windows that means preferring a natural/neural voice over the old SAPI5 ones. Pick from the dropdown in Navy's Settings panel, which lists what this machine actually has; a name that isn't installed is ignored and the automatic choice is used instead.

navy.speechRate.description: Read Aloud playback speed. Above about 1.3 most voices start clipping consonants, which costs comprehension rather than saving time.

navy.maxContextChars.description: Maximum characters of the active file or selection to include as context.

enumDescriptions: Apply file edits automatically without confirmation
Show every file edit in a diff view and ask for confirmation
navy.approvalMode.description: How Navy Coder should handle file edits.

enumDescriptions: Return SEARCH/REPLACE blocks for surgical edits
Return the complete new file content
navy.editFormat.description: Format the model should use when editing files.

navy.maxToolIterations.description: Maximum number of tool-use iterations Navy Coder can perform in one turn.

navy.fileEditSoftCap.description: Writes to the SAME file in one turn before Navy stops feeding fresh diagnostics back and nudges the model to wrap up. Raising it lets a genuine single-file refactor keep going, at the cost of letting a model that is thrashing on one file burn more tokens before anything intervenes.

navy.fileEditHardCap.description: Writes to the SAME file in one turn after which Navy refuses further writes to it for the rest of the turn. This is the backstop against an edit loop, so raising it trades that protection for room to work — a model stuck rewriting one file will make that many attempts before being stopped. Values below the soft cap are raised to match it.

navy.projectRoot.markdownDescription: Pin Navy to a specific project directory. Leave empty for the normal behaviour — Navy remembers the project you last chose per window and defaults to the first workspace folder otherwise, without writing anything to your repository. Set this only to override that; editing it switches Navy immediately.

navy.inlineCompletions.description: Enable ghost-text inline completions as you type. Uses the active provider and model (or navy.completionModel if set). Triggers after a 350ms debounce.

navy.completionModel.markdownDescription: Separate, faster model to use for inline ghost-text completions only — leave empty to reuse `navy.model`. Inline completions need low latency, so pointing this at a small/fast model (e.g. a local Ollama model like `qwen2.5-coder:1.5b`, or a fast hosted model) keeps typing responsive without changing which model handles chat.

navy.embeddingModel.markdownDescription:
Embedding model for semantic codebase search (used by `find_relevant_files` in addition to keyword search). Leave empty to disable — keyword-only search is the default.

**⚠️ Privacy:** enabling this sends the first ~1500 characters of each source file in your project to the embedding provider you have configured. If `navy.provider` is a hosted service (OpenAI, Gemini, …), your code leaves your machine. Files whose names look credential-bearing (`.env*`, `*secret*`, `*credentials*`, `*.pem`, `serviceAccount*`, `docker-compose*`, …) and anything your repo gitignores are excluded, but review the setting before enabling it on a private codebase. Use a local Ollama embedding model (e.g. `nomic-embed-text`) to keep everything on-device.

Must be an embeddings-capable model for the active `navy.provider` (e.g. `nomic-embed-text` or `mxbai-embed-large` for Ollama, `text-embedding-3-small` for OpenAI, `text-embedding-004` for Gemini). The index is built incrementally and cached in `.navy/embeddings/`, which is gitignored automatically; re-indexing a changed file rewrites only the shard it belongs to.

enumDescriptions: Local Ollama instance
LM Studio (local, OpenAI-compatible, http://localhost:1234)
Anthropic Claude (api.anthropic.com)
OpenAI / ChatGPT (api.openai.com)
DeepSeek (api.deepseek.com)
Google Gemini (via OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
xAI Grok (api.x.ai)
z.ai / GLM (api.z.ai/api/paas/v4 — set navy.apiBase to https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4 for a GLM Coding Plan subscription, or https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4 for a mainland-China account)
Groq (api.groq.com)
OpenRouter — multi-provider gateway (openrouter.ai)
Moonshot AI / Kimi (api.moonshot.ai — set navy.apiBase to api.moonshot.cn for the mainland-China endpoint)

Alibaba Qwen via Model Studio / DashScope (dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 — set navy.apiBase to https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 for the mainland-China endpoint; a key issued in one region is not valid in the other)
MiniMax (api.minimax.io — set navy.apiBase to https://api.minimax.chat/v1 for the mainland-China endpoint; the older api.minimaxi.com host is still live but rejects current international keys)
Xiaomi MiMo (api.xiaomimimo.com)
Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (set navy.apiBase)
Local Ollama running on your own machine (navy.host, default http://localhost:11434)
Ollama Cloud (ollama.com) — no local install needed, requires an API key
navy.ollamaMode.markdownDescription:
Which Ollama to talk to when `navy.provider` is `ollama`.

`local` uses the server at `navy.host` and needs Ollama installed.

`cloud` talks to **https://ollama.com** instead, so nothing has to be installed locally — you only need an API key from your Ollama account, saved with the key icon next to the model picker (stored in the OS keychain, never in settings). Ollama Cloud runs large models that would not fit on most machines.

navy.apiBase.description: Base URL override for the provider API (e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1). Used when provider is 'custom' or to override a built-in provider's URL.

enumDescriptions: Lowest latency — minimal reasoning (temperature 0, no extended thinking)
Balanced (default)
Deepest reasoning — extended thinking on Claude, high reasoning effort on o-series, think mode on Ollama reasoning models
navy.thinkingLevel.description: How much reasoning effort the model should spend per request.

navy.searchApiKey.description: API key for web search. Tavily keys start with 'tvly-'; any other non-empty value is treated as a Brave Search key. Leave empty to use DuckDuckGo (no key required).

navy.codeLens.description: Show 'Ask Navy' code lens buttons above functions in the editor.

enumDescriptions: Commands run directly on your machine (current behavior)
Commands run inside a Docker container built from the project's own .devcontainer/Dockerfile, with only the project folder mounted
navy.sandboxMode.markdownDescription:
Isolate `run_command`/`run_tests`/`run_project`/background processes inside a Docker container instead of running them directly on your machine. Requires Docker to be installed and running, and the project to have a `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` or `Dockerfile` — Navy refuses to guess at a generic image, since a container that doesn't actually match the project's real toolchain would be a false sense of safety. This is a second, independent layer on top of the approval dialog and workspace-trust check, not a replacement for either.

Works on Windows, macOS and Linux. With sandboxing on, Navy targets the container rather than the host: commands are written for and run through POSIX `sh` even from a Windows host, since that is what the container actually provides.

enumDescriptions: Reduce automatically for small local models (local Ollama / LM Studio when the model name suggests ≤9B parameters or the effective context window is ≤16k tokens)
Always offer the reduced core set, on every provider and model
Always offer every tool (the behavior of previous versions)
navy.reducedToolset.markdownDescription: Offer small models a reduced core tool set instead of all ~37 tools. The full tool schemas ride along on **every** request — several thousand tokens that a small local model pays out of an already-small window, and a longer menu measurably worsens tool *choice* on small models. The core set keeps the read → edit → verify loop, search/retrieval, run/test, git status/diff, and skills; everything else (renames, deletes, git history, web access, background processes, LSP symbol tools, delegation) is withheld but listed in the prompt, and the model unlocks all of it mid-turn with one `request_more_tools` call when the task needs it. This is a context optimisation, never a permission change: an unlocked tool goes through exactly the same approval gate as always. The Output panel says when a turn ran reduced.

navy.contextWindow.markdownDescription: Context window to use, in tokens. `0` (the default) means **Max** — whatever the current model actually reports, so it follows the model automatically instead of being pinned to a number that stops being right the moment you switch. Pick a smaller size from the dropdown next to the model picker when the maximum is more than you want: for Ollama this is sent as `num_ctx` and directly controls how much memory the KV cache reserves, so lowering it is the fix if a large-window local model loads slowly or offloads to CPU. For hosted providers the window is fixed by the API and can't be changed from here — a smaller value there only tells Navy to treat the conversation as full sooner. Always clamped to what the model actually supports.

navy.mcpServers.markdownDescription: MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool servers Navy can use, same format as Claude Desktop. Local (stdio) example: `{ "windbg": { "command": "pwsh.exe", "args": ["-File", "C:/path/server.ps1"] } }`. Remote (streamable HTTP) example: `{ "myserver": { "url": "https://example.com/mcp" } }`. Tools appear to the agent as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`.

command.description: Executable to launch a local (stdio) MCP server.

env.description: Extra environment variables for a local server.

url.description: Endpoint URL for a remote (streamable HTTP) MCP server. Use this instead of command/args/env.

headers.description: Extra HTTP headers for a remote server (e.g. Authorization).

navy.providerFallbacks.markdownDescription: Backup providers to try, in order, if the primary provider (`navy.provider`/`navy.model`) fails with a rate limit, a server outage, or a network error — never for an API-key/auth problem, a quota/billing limit, or a conversation too large for the model, since those need YOU to fix something rather than a different account to silently pay for. Empty by default — opt-in only. Each entry needs its own API key already saved (the key icon next to the model picker) for its provider; Navy always says plainly in the chat when a fallback actually runs, including which provider handled the request, so you're never surprised by what ran or which account it billed. Example: `[{ "provider": "anthropic", "model": "claude-sonnet-5" }, { "provider": "ollama", "model": "llama3", "host": "http://localhost:11434" }]`.

provider.description: Provider id — same values as navy.provider (ollama, anthropic, openai, gemini, deepseek, xai, zai, groq, openrouter, moonshot, qwen, minimax, mimo, lmstudio, custom).

model.description: Model to use with this fallback provider.

apiBase.description: Optional API base override for this fallback (same meaning as navy.apiBase).

host.description: Optional inference server URL, only used when provider is "ollama" or "lmstudio" (same meaning as navy.host).

navy.persistBackgroundProcesses.markdownDescription: Let `run_project`/`start_process` background processes survive closing or reloading this window instead of being stopped when it does. Off by default — with this off, nothing changes. When on, those processes are simply never told to stop, and their output is written to a log file under `.navy/bg-logs/` instead of streamed live to the chat, since there is no longer anything on this end reading it once the window that started them is gone (`read_process_output` reads the log file's current contents either way). Reopening a project that still has one of these running offers to stop it, so a background process you forgot about doesn't run forever unnoticed.
